BIRLA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY, MESRA, RANCHI
(MID SEMESTER EXAMINATION)

CLASS: BE   SEMESTER: III
BRANCH: CIVIL   SESSION : MO/2018

SUBJECT : CE3003-SURVEYING - I

TIME: 1.5  HOURS   FULL MARKS: 25

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. The total marks of the questions are 30.
2. Candidates may attempt for all 30 marks.
3. In those cases where the marks obtained exceed 25 marks, the excess will be ignored.
4. Before attempting the question paper, be sure that you have got the correct question paper.
5. The missing data, if any, may be assumed suitably.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------



Q1 (a) What are the principles of surveying? [2]
 (b) On a map drawn to a scale of 50 m to 1 cm, a surveyor measured the distance between
two stations as 3500 m. But later, it was found that by mistake he had used a scale of 100
m to 1 cm. Find the true distance between the stations.
[3]


Q2 (a) What are the classifications of survey?  [2]
 (b) An old map was plotted to a scale of 40 m to 1 cm. Over the years, the map has been
shrinking, and a line originally 20 cm long is only 19.5 cm long at present. If the present
area of the map measured by planimeter is 125.50 cm
2
, find the true area of the land
surveyed.
[3]


Q3  A steel tape was exactly 20 m long at 20°C when supported throughout its length under a
pull  of  5  kg.  A  line  measured  with  this  tape  under  a  pull  of  16  kg  and  at  a  mean
temperature  of  32°C,  was  found  to  be  680  m  long.  Assuming  the  tape  is  supported  at
every 20 m, find the true  length of the line. Given  that (i) Cross-sectional area of the
tape = 0.03 cm
2
, (ii) E = 2.1 x 10
6
 kg/cm
2
, (iii) α = 11 x 10
-6
per °C, and (iv)density of the
tape = 10 g/c.c.
[5]


Q4 (a) List the obstacles in chain survey? [2]
 (b) Explain the working principle of optical square with proper figure. [3]


Q5 (a) What is local attraction? [2]
 (b) Convert the following W.C.B. to R.B. or vice versa: (i) 123°17’, (ii) S 74°32’ W,
(iii) N 13°21’ E.
[3]


Q6  A closed traverse is conducted with five stations A, B, C, D and E taken in anticlockwise
order, in the form of a regular pentagon. If the F.B. of AB is 30°00’, Find the F.B. of the
other sides.
[5]
